source.title: Incentivizing Strong Reasoning from Weak Supervision
source.authors: Yige Yuan; Teng Xiao; Shuchang Tao; Xue Wang; Jin-Yang Gao; Bo-Lin Ding; Bing-Bing Xu

record.file_problem: No apparent garbling or cutoff; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether SFT on weaker models’ reasoning traces improves stronger students, but uses long chain-of-thought supervision and an RL-relative RGR metric rather than the original study’s label setup and PGR measure.
record.gate_note: The study reports comparisons of weak teachers, base students, SFT students, and RL-trained students. Table 2 separately reports Pass@1 by student, benchmark, and training variant; rows below cover W2SR and W2SR-P. Table 1 is flattened and its remaining cells cannot be reliably assigned. Figure-only results are not transcribed where the text does not provide assignable values.
record.test_reason: Strong Qwen2.5 students (7B-Math, 14B, 32B) are SFT'd on long-CoT traces from smaller RL-trained Qwen2.5 teachers and compared with the teacher, the vanilla student and an RL-trained student. Comparing student with teacher is a direct V1 test, though by a different method: long-CoT imitation rather than weak labels, and an RL-trained student rather than a true-label model as ceiling (RGR, not PGR). Answer-correctness filtering (W2SR-P) is a training change bearing on V2. Teacher type and scale comparisons bear on V3.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly accurate. The authors conclude that traces from much weaker reasoner teachers substantially improve stronger students, recovering up to ~94% of RL gains at far lower cost. They find teacher reasoning ability matters more than size or accuracy, incorrect traces still help, and teacher scale has diminishing returns. They state students consistently outperform their weak teachers; their own Tables 1-2 contradict this for some close-size pairs.
record.recipe_differences: Uses SFT on long chain-of-thought traces from weaker reasoning models, with W2SR, correct-only W2SR-P, and incorrect-only W2SR-N variants. Its RGR compares against an RL-trained student rather than measuring Burns et al.’s PGR against a true-label-trained ceiling.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by benchmark, student size, teacher type, and whether trajectories are filtered to correct answers. Correct-only filtering is not uniformly better than using all trajectories.

fits_no_version.finding: W2SR raises average response length (e.g. 882.78 to 1545.92 tokens for 7B-Math) and cuts training time about 25x vs GRPO.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weak-teacher CoT distillation induces inference-time scaling and is cheaper than RL.

record.code_released: The paper says code is publicly available at a link, but no URL is stated in the provided text.
record.peer_reviewed: Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported. The primary table is flattened in the supplied text, preventing reliable extraction of many Table 1 values. The authors state that the work focuses on mathematical reasoning and broader-domain effectiveness remains unverified.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2 W2SR-N results are not included as separate rows; the table’s many incorrect-only condition results would exceed the extraction focus on W2SR and W2SR-P. Table 1’s remaining model/benchmark values and RGR cells are omitted because the flattened layout does not reliably assign them. Figure 3 and other figures are not exhaustively transcribed where exact values are not stated in the text.

untested.parts: Original setup: weak-label classification fine-tuning and a ceiling trained on ground-truth labels (PGR). Here the ceiling is an RL-trained student.
Auxiliary confidence loss, ensembling of weak supervisors, loss variants; only answer-correctness filtering of teacher traces is tested.
Chess and reward-modelling tasks; representation-based predictors of PGR; non-Qwen model families.
Entire version: exploitation of unverifiable supervisor errors, distribution shift, correlated errors.

missing.what: Teacher Pass@1, W2SR/W2SR-P Pass@1 and RGR for the other teacher-student pairs: 0.5B(R) to 7B-Math, 1.5B(R) to 14B, 1.5B(R) and 7B(R) to 32B, plus GRPO ceilings
Diminishing returns from teacher scale: with a 32B student, 1.5B to 7B teacher gives +11.4% on MATH, 7B to 32B only +0.4%
Non-reasoner 32B teacher yields students worse than the teacher on Minerva and AMC (-2.41%, -5.88% relative); the 1.5B reasoner teacher improves them
W2SR-N (incorrect-only traces) student scores vs teacher and vanilla, e.g. 7B-Math average 43.77 vs vanilla 30.71

record.verdict_notes: RGR uses an RL-trained student as the ceiling. When the teacher beats that ceiling (32B/14B Minerva), RGR reads 200%+ even though the student is below its teacher, so RGR should not be read as PGR. Tables 1 and 2 disagree for the 14B/7B W2SR cells (e.g. MATH 80.00 vs 78.80), and the text cites 53.53 where Table 2 gives 53.18. No uncertainty is reported, and AMC has 40 items, so 2.5 points is one question. 'Weak' teachers are weak in size; the 7B(R) and 14B(R) teachers often outperform the vanilla students.

versions.untested_parts: The study uses RGR relative to an RL-trained student, not PGR relative to a strong student trained on true labels. It does not test the original label-supervision setup.
Tests filtering to correct-answer trajectories (W2SR-P) against all trajectories (W2SR); does not test auxiliary confidence loss, ensembling weak supervisors, or loss variants.

Tests several Qwen student sizes, teacher sizes/types, and reasoning benchmarks. Does not test representation-based predictors, and the text does not provide extractable numerical values for all teacher-scale comparisons.
Does not test distribution shift, students exploiting what supervisors cannot check, or whether gains shrink when teacher and student errors are alike.
No theoretical conditions for a student necessarily beating its supervisor are tested.
